status_note: No trained model exists, so none of these thresholds has ever been fitted to data. They are conservative starting points, not measured operating points.
candidate_note: The decode/NMS score floor, deliberately BELOW minimum_detection_score. A detection between the two bars is something the model saw but cannot report: it reaches the decision policy and becomes UNABLE_TO_ASSESS / LOW_CONFIDENCE. If this floor were equal to minimum_detection_score, the low-confidence abstention branch would be unreachable and the system would silently answer NO_TARGET_MARKER_DETECTED for a weak sighting.
minimum_detection_note: The reporting bar. At or above this, a recognised class becomes a visible marker in the response.
iou_note: Ultralytics uses 0.7 in validation and 0.45 on the prediction path. One value is pinned here so a result is reproducible; this is the prediction-path value.
multi_label_note: Ultralytics enables multi_label during validation, which lets one box emit one detection per class. That would corrupt the two-marker decision logic, so it stays off.
